summary: SSE keepalive misalignment + edge proxy coalescing causes silent stall mid-stream
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (surface first with NoteCraft on Dedicated) report SSE streaming chat sessions going silent mid-generation while the server continues to process the request. Connection remains ESTABLISHED, no 5xx returned, and token counts on the server indicate generation continued. Impact: user-facing chat UIs show a stalled response and eventually trigger client-side timeouts. Environment: Dedicated pool in prod/us-east behind Fastly edge + Nginx reverse proxy (customer-managed).

Observed behavior differs from prior streaming stalls: TCP stays open and no FIN/RST; application logs show continuous token emission in runtime, but nothing reaches client until the end of generation (or until a subsequent small flush).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer SDK opens SSE connection to /v1/chat/stream with common headers.
2) Start a generation with long content (estimated > 400 tokens).
3) Observe streaming stall mid-generation (client silent) despite server token generation continuing.
4) Reproduce is reliable when request path traverses Fastly + Nginx with gzip_enabled=true on the proxy.

Note: Reproduction is intermittent on plain internet paths (depends on middlebox behavior).
logs:
Sample request_id: rq_20260310_07a3b2c4
Serving-runtime trace: generation-start=2026-03-10T15:18:06Z, last-token-emitted=2026-03-10T15:18:24Z, generation-end=2026-03-10T15:18:26Z
Gateway-side: sse-outbound-flushes at 15:18:06, 15:18:26 (no intermediate chunk flush).
Fastly edge logs show coalesced backend responses and occasional small cache-miss buffering. Nginx access logs contain upstream_response_time spikes aligning with the silent period.
SDK client log: receives initial event headers, then no chunks until final event. No connection resets.
Correlated metrics: 95p latency for streaming token flush spikes at same timestamps.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: middlebox/proxy is buffering small SSE chunks and emitting only when buffer thresholds or timed flushes are hit, causing perceived mid-stream silence. Confirmed: when we forced server to emit comment keep-alive every 2s (':ping\n\n') client received keepalives and UI stayed responsive.
Further tracing shows SDKs expecting periodic ping frames around 3s; customer proxies performing gzip/coalescing combine several tiny chunks into a single TCP write which delays client visibility. Fastly + Nginx combination with gzip_on and proxy_buffering default led to coalescing.
We reproduced in lab by inserting Nginx with proxy_buffering on and gzip; same behavior.
Additional discovery: a recent serving-runtime change (PR #2121) removed periodic empty-comment keepalive in favor of relying on connection-level TCP keepalive; this reduced network-level flushes and exposed proxy buffering regressions.
comments: NoteCraft engineer (2026-03-10): 'We see the UI freeze ~10s into the response for long replies. No errors in console, socket still open.'
Support (Lina) (2026-03-10): 'Thank you — can you share proxy chain (CDN/proxy) and an example request_id? Also set SDK debug logs please.'
SRE (Marcus) (2026-03-11): 'Added temporary diagnostic flag to emit explicit SSE comments every 2s for affected customers; this confirmed the problem is buffer coalescing at the proxy layer.'

Eng (Priya Rao) (2026-03-11): 'PR 2345 adds configurable sse_keepalive_interval and explicitly writes zero-length comment frames to force flushes. Also added docs recommending disabling gzip for SSE endpoints at reverse proxies.'
Support (Lina) (2026-03-12): 'NoteCraft validated workaround: toggling proxy gzip off restored continuous token flow. They will apply config change while we roll out runtime patch.'
resolution:
Mitigation: documented proxy config recommendations for SSE (disable gzip compression for streaming endpoints, set proxy_buffering off, or lower proxy flush thresholds). Workaround: enable SDK fallback to WebSocket streaming for affected customers or set server sse_keepalive_interval=2000ms (temporary diagnostic flag).
Fix: merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2345 which restores periodic SSE empty-comment keepalives and exposes a config option sse_keepalive_interval. Rollout: feature flag enabled for dedicated pools in prod/us-east on 2026-03-12 canary; monitoring shows resolved behavior for NoteCraft.
Follow-ups: update SDKs to surface keepalive config; add automated regression test that runs SSE stream through a proxy stack (Fastly+Nginx) in CI; create runbook entry for customer-facing guidance.
